goal.en: Say how certain you are, and talk about the past you cannot change.
goal.ar: أن تعبّر عن درجة يقينك، وأن تتحدث عن ماضٍ لا يمكن تغييره.

title.en: must be, might be, can't be

text.en: These modals show how sure you are, not what is permitted: must be (I am sure it is), might/could be (possible), can't be (I am sure it is not).
text.ar: هذه الأفعال تعبّر عن درجة يقينك لا عن الإذن: must be أي «متأكد أنه كذلك»، وmight/could be أي «ربما»، وcan't be أي «متأكد أنه ليس كذلك».

head: Certainty
Modal
Example
rows: He must be at work — his car has gone.
She might be in the library.
That can't be Omar — he is in Cairo.

text.en: The opposite of “must be” is “can't be”, not “mustn't be”. “Mustn't” means it is forbidden.
text.ar: نقيض must be هو can't be وليس mustn't be، لأن mustn't تعني المنع لا نفي اليقين.

title.en: must have, might have, can't have

text.en: modal + have + past participle talks about certainty in the past: “She must have left early.”
text.ar: الفعل الناقص مع have والتصريف الثالث يعبّر عن اليقين في الماضي: She must have left early.

items.en: The ground is wet — it must have rained.
items.ar: الأرض مبللة، لا بد أنها أمطرت.

items.en: He might have forgotten the meeting.
She can't have finished already — it's too soon.
items.ar: مستحيل أن تكون قد انتهت، فالوقت مبكر جداً.

text.en: In speech “have” sounds like “of” — but never write “must of”. It is always “must have” or “must've”.
text.ar: في النطق تشبه have كلمة of، لكن لا تكتب must of أبداً. الصواب must have أو must've.

text.en: should have + past participle criticises or regrets a past action: “I should have studied harder.” The negative: “You shouldn't have told him.”
text.ar: should have مع التصريف الثالث تعبّر عن الندم أو اللوم على فعل ماضٍ: I should have studied harder. والنفي: You shouldn't have told him.

head: Form
Meaning
rows: I didn't call, and I regret it.
You paid, and that was a mistake.
It was necessary, and I did it.
It was not necessary, so maybe I didn't.

text.en: “Must” has no past. For past obligation use “had to”: “I had to work on Saturday”, not “I musted”.
text.ar: لا ماضي للفعل must. وللتعبير عن إلزام ماضٍ نستخدم had to: I had to work on Saturday.

questions.sentence: The lights are on, so someone ___ at home.

explanation.en: Evidence points to a confident conclusion → must be.
explanation.ar: الدليل يقود إلى استنتاج واثق، فنستخدم must be.

questions.sentence: That ___ be Sara — she flew to Amman this morning.

explanation.en: Confident that it is NOT true → can't be. “Mustn't” would mean it is forbidden.
explanation.ar: يقين بأن الأمر غير صحيح، فنستخدم can't be. أما mustn't فتعني المنع.

questions.sentence: I'm not sure where he is. He ___ be in the lab.

explanation.ar: عدم اليقين يقتضي احتمالاً، فنستخدم might.

options: That mustn't be his brother at all.
That can't be his brother — he has no brother.
He must be tired after that long trip.
She might be waiting for us downstairs.

explanation.en: To say you are sure something is not true, use “can't be”. “Mustn't” expresses prohibition.
explanation.ar: لنفي اليقين نستخدم can't be، أما mustn't فتعبّر عن المنع.

questions.sentence: The streets are wet. It ___ during the night.

explanation.en: Present evidence about a past event → must have + past participle.
explanation.ar: دليل حاضر على حدث ماضٍ، فنستخدم must have مع التصريف الثالث.

questions.sentence: She ___ my message — she never replied.

explanation.en: A possible explanation for something in the past → might not have + participle.
explanation.ar: تفسير محتمل لحدث ماضٍ، فنستخدم might not have مع التصريف الثالث.

options: He must of left his keys at home.
He must have left his keys at home.
She might have missed the early train.
They can't have arrived so quickly.

explanation.en: “Must of” is a spelling of the spoken sound; the written form is “must have”.
explanation.ar: عبارة must of كتابة خاطئة لصوت النطق، والصواب must have.

prompt.en: “They can't have known about the change.” What does the speaker believe?
prompt.ar: «They can't have known about the change» بماذا يعتقد المتكلم؟

options: They were certainly unaware of it.
They were forbidden from knowing it.
They possibly knew about it already.
They will find out about it later.

explanation.en: “Can't have” is a confident negative conclusion about the past.
explanation.ar: can't have استنتاج منفي واثق عن الماضي.

questions.sentence: I failed the test. I ___ harder.

explanation.en: Regret about the past → should have + past participle.
explanation.ar: ندم على الماضي، فنستخدم should have مع التصريف الثالث.

prompt.en: “You shouldn't have paid for dinner.” What happened?
prompt.ar: «You shouldn't have paid for dinner» ماذا حدث؟

options: He paid, and the speaker thinks he needn't have.
He didn't pay, and that was wrong of him.
He will pay for dinner later tonight.
He was not allowed to pay for dinner.

explanation.en: “Shouldn't have” always describes something that DID happen and is now being judged.
explanation.ar: shouldn't have تصف دائماً شيئاً وقع فعلاً ويُحكم عليه الآن.

questions.sentence: I ___ work last Saturday because of the deadline.

explanation.en: Past obligation that actually happened → had to. “Must” has no past form.
explanation.ar: إلزام ماضٍ وقع فعلاً، فنستخدم had to، إذ لا ماضي لـ must.

prompt.en: Which sentence says the payment was NOT necessary?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تفيد أن الدفع لم يكن ضرورياً؟

options: We didn't have to pay for parking.
We mustn't have paid for parking.
We shouldn't have paid for parking.
We had to pay for parking there.

explanation.en: “Didn't have to” removes the obligation. “Shouldn't have” says we paid and it was a mistake.
explanation.ar: didn't have to ترفع الإلزام، أما shouldn't have فتعني أننا دفعنا وكان ذلك خطأ.

prompt.en: Match the modal with the degree of certainty.

explanation.en: The same modals do two jobs — certainty and obligation. Context decides which.
explanation.ar: الأفعال نفسها تؤدي وظيفتين: اليقين والإلزام، والسياق هو الذي يحدد المقصود.

questions.answer: She must have forgotten about the meeting

explanation.ar: الفعل الناقص ثم have ثم التصريف الثالث.

prompt.en: Express regret: “I didn't book a table.” → “I ___ a table.”
prompt.ar: عبّر عن الندم: I didn't book a table ← I ___ a table.

explanation.en: should have + past participle turns a past fact into a regret.
explanation.ar: should have مع التصريف الثالث تحوّل الحقيقة الماضية إلى ندم.
